events.title: Erased but Recoverable: On the Fragility of Concept Erasure Under Fine-Tuning
events.summary: A new research paper examines how well concept erasure in open-source text-to-image diffusion models survives later fine-tuning. It finds that common adaptation techniques such as DreamBooth, LoRA, or Custom Diffusion can reshape a model's internal representations and weaken or reverse previously erased concepts, and it proposes treating erasure persistence as an important property to study.
events.why_it_matters: The record shows that safety filters relying on concept erasure may not hold once models are fine-tuned, meaning erased or restricted content can resurface. Developers and organisations deploying customised open-source diffusion models should therefore treat erasure as fragile and re-verify safety behaviour after adaptation.

events.why_it_matters: Teams running self-hosted source control can now enable code scanning without exposing their networks to the public AWS IP range, reducing firewall exposure. The automatic fix pull request feature may shorten remediation time for code findings.

events.title: AWS Continuum for Penetration Testing now supports pause and resume
events.summary: Amazon has added pause-and-resume capability to its AI-driven penetration testing service for web applications and APIs, letting a stopped or failed test pick up from a checkpoint instead of restarting from scratch. Previously a job that failed had to be rerun completely, repeating work already done.
events.why_it_matters: This is a workflow improvement for security teams using the AWS service, reducing wasted time when a test job is interrupted by a configuration error. It preserves findings and completed work from earlier in the run. The record reports no security vulnerability or exploitation.

events.title: AWS Site-to-Site VPN now supports post-quantum key exchanges
events.summary: AWS has added support for post-quantum key exchange methods in its Site-to-Site VPN service, letting customers enable them in IPsec tunnel settings via existing APIs, aligned with NIST migration guidance, at no extra charge.
events.why_it_matters: Post-quantum key exchange addresses the risk that encrypted traffic captured today could be decrypted later once quantum computers mature. Defenders connecting offices or data centres to AWS can enable it as part of PQC migration planning, at no additional cost.

events.title: AWS STS announces GetScopedCredentials to scope down permissions at runtime
events.summary: AWS has launched a new Security Token Service API, GetScopedCredentials, that lets users derive temporary credentials with reduced permissions and session duration from credentials they already hold. The scoped credentials keep the caller's identity while narrowing access for agents, sub-agents, and workloads.
events.why_it_matters: This gives defenders a native AWS mechanism to apply least-privilege downscoping to temporary credentials, which helps contain the blast radius if an agent or workload is compromised. Because the narrowed credentials preserve the caller's identity, attribution of actions stays intact while permissions can only shrink, never expand.

events.title: Who Is Behind the Harness? Verifying Model Identity in Coding Agents through Behavioral Fingerprinting
events.summary: Researchers introduce LIDAR, a technique for identifying which language model is running behind a coding-agent harness by analysing its behaviour rather than raw text or token statistics. The motivation is that swapping the model behind an agent can alter security-relevant decisions, and conventional fingerprints break down when signals are mediated by instructions, tools and execution feedback.
events.why_it_matters: The paper argues that the identity of the model inside a coding agent affects whether changes are properly verified and failures recovered from safely, so unverified model substitution is a security concern. It gives defenders a behavioural method to check which model is actually behind an agent when text-based fingerprints no longer transfer.
